description: A simple PCIe request-response controller that handles incoming requests and generates corresponding responses. The controller accepts a request signal and outputs a response signal after a fixed delay.
code:
module pcie_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input req,
    output reg rsp
);

    reg [2:0] state;
    
    parameter IDLE = 3'b000, REQUEST = 3'b001, RESPONSE = 3'b010;
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            rsp <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (req) begin
                        state <= REQUEST;
                    end
                end
                REQUEST: begin
                    state <= RESPONSE;
                end
                RESPONSE: begin
                    rsp <= 1; // Generate response
                    state <= IDLE; // Go back to IDLE
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Design an 8-bit deserializer that takes in a serial input signal and outputs the corresponding 8-bit parallel signal. The deserializer should read one bit per clock cycle and latch the bits into an 8-bit output register once 8 bits have been received. The deserializer also includes a reset signal that initializes the output register to zero.

module deserializer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire serial_in,
    output reg [7:0] parallel_out,
    output reg data_ready
);
    reg [2:0] bit_count; // To count the number of bits received

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            parallel_out <= 8'b0;
            bit_count <= 3'b0;
            data_ready <= 1'b0;
        end else if (bit_count < 3'd8) begin
            parallel_out[bit_count] <= serial_in; // Store the bit
            bit_count <= bit_count + 1; // Increment the bit count
            data_ready <= 1'b0; // Not ready yet
        end else begin
            data_ready <= 1'b1; // Data is ready after 8 bits
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a fixed-priority arbiter in Verilog. The arbiter should handle three request signals (req0, req1, req2) and grant a single output (grant) based on fixed priority: req0 > req1 > req2. When a request is granted, the arbiter should also remember the last granted request and only grant the same request again if it is still active and has the highest priority.
code:
module fixed_priority_arbiter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire req0,
    input wire req1,
    input wire req2,
    output reg grant
);

reg [1:0] last_grant;

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    if (rst) begin
        grant <= 0;
        last_grant <= 2'b00; // No request granted
    end else begin
        if (req0) begin
            grant <= 1'b1; // Grant req0
            last_grant <= 2'b00;
        end else if (req1 && last_grant != 2'b00) begin
            grant <= 1'b1; // Grant req1 if last was not req0
            last_grant <= 2'b01;
        end else if (req2 && last_grant == 2'b01) begin
            grant <= 1'b1; // Grant req2 if last was req1
            last_grant <= 2'b10;
        end else begin
            grant <= 1'b0; // No grant
        end
    end
end

endmodule

Design a Verilog module for a crystal oscillator that generates a square wave clock signal. The oscillator should have an adjustable frequency controlled by a 3-bit frequency select input. The output clock should toggle its state based on the selected frequency. The oscillator should also include a reset input that initializes the output clock to 0.
code:
module crystal_oscillator(
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [2:0] freq_select,
    output reg clk_out
);
    reg [23:0] counter;
    reg [23:0] freq_divisor;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            clk_out <= 0;
            counter <= 0;
            freq_divisor <= 24'd1000000; // Default frequency divisor
        end else begin
            // Adjust frequency divisor based on freq_select
            case (freq_select)
                3'b000: freq_divisor <= 24'd1000000; // 1 MHz
                3'b001: freq_divisor <= 24'd500000;  // 2 MHz
                3'b010: freq_divisor <= 24'd333333;  // 3 MHz
                3'b011: freq_divisor <= 24'd250000;  // 4 MHz
                3'b100: freq_divisor <= 24'd200000;  // 5 MHz
                default: freq_divisor <= 24'd1000000; // Default
            endcase
            
            // Counter logic
            if (counter < (freq_divisor >> 1)) begin
                counter <= counter + 1;
            end else begin
                clk_out <= ~clk_out; // Toggle clock output
                counter <= 0; // Reset counter
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

Design an IIR filter in Verilog that takes a 16-bit input sample and outputs a 16-bit filtered sample. The filter coefficients should be defined as parameters. The filter should implement a simple one-pole IIR filter defined by the equation: 
output[n] = b0 * input[n] + a1 * output[n-1], where b0 and a1 are the filter coefficients. The design should include a clock and reset signal for synchronous operation.

module iir_filter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [15:0] x, // input sample
    output reg [15:0] y // output sample
);

    parameter a1 = 16'h1FFF; // example coefficient

    reg [15:0] y_prev;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            y <= 16'b0;
            y_prev <= 16'b0;
        end else begin
            y <= (b0 * x + a1 * y_prev) >> 15; // Implement the filter equation
            y_prev <= y; // Store previous output

endmodule

Design a convolutional encoder with a constraint length of 3 and a rate of 1/2. The encoder should take a 1-bit input and produce two 1-bit outputs based on the following generator polynomials:

- G2: 101 (i.e., the polynomial represents \(x^2 + 1\))
The state of the encoder should be represented by a 2-bit register, and the output should be computed whenever there is a new input.

module convolutional_encoder(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input input_bit,
    output reg output_bit1,
    output reg output_bit2
);

        if (rst) begin
            state <= 2'b00;
            output_bit1 <= 0;
            output_bit2 <= 0;
        end else begin
            // Compute the next state
            output_bit1 <= input_bit ^ state[0] ^ state[1]; // G1: 111

description: Implement a Monte Carlo simulation for estimating the value of π using a combinational logic circuit. The circuit should take a number of random points generated in a 2D space (x, y) and check if they fall within a unit circle. The output should be the ratio of points inside the circle to the total points multiplied by 4, which estimates π.
code:
module monte_carlo_pi(
    input [7:0] x, // x-coordinate (0 to 255)
    input [7:0] y, // y-coordinate (0 to 255)
    input [7:0] total_points, // total number of points
    output reg [31:0] pi_estimate // estimated value of π
);
    wire inside_circle;
    assign inside_circle = (x * x + y * y) <= (255 * 255); // Check if inside unit circle

    always @(*) begin
        if (total_points > 0) begin
            pi_estimate = (inside_circle ? 1 : 0) * 4 / total_points; // Estimate π
        end else begin
            pi_estimate = 0; // Handle zero total points case
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple Watchdog Timer in Verilog. The timer should have an input for a reset signal and a clock signal. When the timer is not reset for a certain number of clock cycles, it will signal an output indicating a timeout. The timer should reset when the reset signal is high.

Design a simple PCIe endpoint that receives a request signal, processes it, and then sends a response signal after a fixed latency. );

description: Design a Verilog module that implements a simple SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) system for a robot. description: Design a Verilog module that performs Huffman encoding for a given set of characters and their frequencies. description:

- 01: 0011 (Medium Voltage & Frequency)

);

            2'b10: voltage_frequency <= 4'b0110; // High Voltage & Frequency

end

    output reg done
);

    reg [31:0] data; // Store data for serialization

            serial_out <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            data <= 0;

            data <= data_in; // Load data on start
            bit_count <= 0; // Reset bit count

        end else if (bit_count < 32) begin
            serial_out <= data[31 - bit_count]; // Output the current bit
            bit_count <= bit_count + 1; // Increment bit count

    output reg prediction // Prediction output

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // Initialize state to Strongly not taken
            prediction <= 1'b0; // Prediction output
        end else begin
            case (state)
                2'b00: begin
                    if (taken) begin
                        state <= 2'b01; // Move to Weakly not taken
                    end
                    prediction <= 1'b0; // Predict not taken
                end
                2'b01: begin
                    if (taken) begin
                        state <= 2'b10; // Move to Weakly taken
                    end else begin
                        state <= 2'b00; // Move to Strongly not taken
                    end
                    prediction <= 1'b0; // Predict not taken

                    if (taken) begin
                        state <= 2'b11; // Move to Strongly taken
                    end else begin
                        state <= 2'b01; // Move to Weakly not taken
                    end
                    prediction <= 1'b1; // Predict taken
                end
                2'b11: begin
                    if (taken) begin
                        state <= 2'b11; // Stay in Strongly taken

    output reg mosi, // Master Out Slave In
    input wire miso // Master In Slave Out

    reg [3:0] bit_count;
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;

               START = 3'b001,
               SHIFT = 3'b010,
               STOP = 3'b011;

        if (enable) begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    cs <= 1'b0; // Assert chip select
                    shift_reg <= data_in; // Load data into shift register
                    bit_count <= 4'b0000; // Reset bit count
                    state <= START; // Move to START state

                START: begin
                    mosi <= shift_reg[7]; // Send the most significant bit
                    shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
                    state <= SHIFT; // Move to SHIFT state

                SHIFT: begin

                        bit_count <= bit_count + 1; // Increment count

                        state <= STOP; // Move to STOP state
                    end
                end
                STOP: begin
                    cs <= 1'b1; // Deassert chip select
                    state <= IDLE; // Go back to IDLE state

            endcase

            state <= IDLE; // If not enabled, go to IDLE
            cs <= 1'b1; // Deassert chip select

module wifi_sm(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input start,
    input success,

            state <= IDLE; // Reset to IDLE state

                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) state <= CONNECTING;
                end
                CONNECTING: begin
                    if (success) state <= CONNECTED;
                end
                CONNECTED: begin

module bfs_fsm (

    input rst,
    input [3:0] current_node,
    output reg [3:0] next_node
);

    parameter IDLE = 3'b000, LOAD = 3'b001, VISIT = 3'b010, DONE = 3'b011;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            next_node <= 4'b0000;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (current_node < 4) begin
                        state <= LOAD;
                    end
                end
                LOAD: begin
                    next_node <= current_node; // Load current node
                    state <= VISIT;

                        4'b0000: next_node <= 4'b0001; // Node 0 visits Node 1
                        4'b0001: next_node <= 4'b0010; // Node 1 visits Node 2
                        4'b0010: next_node <= 4'b0011; // Node 2 visits Node 3
                        4'b0011: next_node <= 4'b0100; // Node 3 visits Node 4
                        4'b0100: next_node <= 4'bxxxx; // Node 4 has no next node
                        default: next_node <= 4'bxxxx; // Undefined state

                    state <= DONE;
